author: Hroki Saltbeard
pages: In the oldest days the jarls of the north coast were not buried under the earth but given to the sea. Their longships were dragged out over the ice in winter, loaded with their arms and their gold, and a cairn raised amidships over the body.

When the ice broke in spring the ship went down with its master, and the sea that the Nords call the Sea of Ghosts took one more ghost. Divers say the ships lie there still, shields along their rails.
Leave them be. The old songs say a jarl given to the sea keeps his oath to his crew, and his crew keep theirs to him.
